title: z-index
learningObjectives: Explain z-index and build a practical layout with it.

understand.concept: z-index controls the stack level of a positioned element and certain flex or grid items within the relevant stacking context. A larger integer does not always appear above every smaller value because stacking contexts are compared as groups.
understand.whyItMatters: Unplanned stacking can hide controls, text, or focus indicators. Understand the stacking context first rather than continually increasing z-index values.
understand.analogy: A stacking context is like a group of layers inside a folder: the folder is ordered as a unit relative to other folders.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual flex layout follows the flex formatting algorithm and writing-mode rules.

explain.narrative: The second layer appears above the first within their shared stacking context. Try giving one child a new stacking context and compare.

examples.explanation: The second layer appears above the first within their shared stacking context. Try giving one child a new stacking context and compare.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered demonstration of the layout concept.

practise.guidedTask: Create overlapping cards and explain why a child with z-index:999 may still appear beneath a sibling stacking context.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive component using this concept. Test long labels, narrow widths, and keyboard navigation.
hints: Inspect the flex container and items in developer tools.
Change one axis or alignment property at a time.
Test with translated or longer labels.

questions.prompt: Why might z-index:999 still appear below another element?
options: Because stacking contexts are compared as groups
questions.answer: Because stacking contexts are compared as groups
questions.explanation: A descendant cannot escape its ancestor stacking context's order.

questions.prompt: What should you check when changing flex-direction?

questions.answer: How the main and cross axes change
questions.explanation: Flex alignment is defined relative to the main and cross axes.
